newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-RBA revises Australia dlr trade weight index.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-RBA revises Australia dlr trade weight index.

text.p: The Reserve Bank of Australia said on Monday it had revised the weights used for currencies in the Australian dollar trade weighted index (TWI).
The revisions, which take place from October 1, allow for changes in the country mix of Australia's trade during 1995/96, the central bank said in a statement.

The RBA said trends evident in recent years had continued with the weights of Australia's two main trading partners, the Japan and the U.S., declining once again. Japan's weighting slipped to 19.57 percent from 22.64 last year while the U.S. dollar eased to 15.93 percent of the basket from 16.11.

The RBA said trade between Australia and the Asian region, excluding Japan, had continued to increase in importance, accounting for 42 percent of the index against 40 percent a year ago and 38 percent in 1993/94.

The trade weighted basket is made up of the currencies of25 countries, with the South African rand being a new entry this year. The basket covers more than 90 percent of Australia's two-way merchandise trade.
